objective: Take polynomial chaos past order 2 with an adaptive or sparse basis and band a case in more than five dimensions at tractable cost, starting with the four coefficients the existing five-dimensional study left out of the same flat-plate case
rationale: The current position is precise and its ceiling is structural. The one real chaos study fits a total-degree basis of 21 terms in five dimensions from 42 samples, so it runs at roughly twice oversampling and cannot go further without more solves: the implementation refuses when the term count exceeds the sample count, which is the correct behaviour and is also the wall. Accuracy at order 2 is good, with held-out predictive scores near 0.964, and the sensitivity result is strongly concentrated, with one coefficient carrying a total-effect index near 0.925 and the published ordering for a different regime failing to transfer. That concentration is the reason a sparse basis should pay here rather than a generic argument that it might: when one direction dominates and three contribute below one percent, a full total-degree basis spends most of its terms on directions that do not move the answer, and an adaptive basis is exactly the tool for that. The dimension is available without inventing a case, because the source varies nine coefficients and the study varied five of them, so the same flat plate at the same mesh with all nine is a genuine dimension-greater-than-five case with a measured cost per solve and a measured order-2 answer in a subspace to check against. The arithmetic that makes this a real test rather than a demonstration: a full order-2 basis in nine dimensions is 55 terms, so the naive design needs of order 110 solves, and the claim to beat is banding the same quantity at materially fewer than that. The check that keeps it honest is free, since restricting the nine-dimensional surrogate to the five varied before must reproduce the existing order-2 result within its own held-out error. Axis A: reading-kind, priced from the same case's measured per-solve cost. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured on this exact case and mesh: 44.7 core-min bought 42 solves at the 13,056-cell level restarting from a converged baseline, about 1.06 core-min per solve, so an adaptive design of about 60 solves plus a held-out set of 10 comes to about 70 core-min at the same rank count and concurrency; the naive full order-2 design in nine dimensions would need about 110 solves on the same basis, and that figure is the number this item exists to beat
expected_knowledge_gain: Three outcomes. One: the adaptive basis bands the nine-dimensional case at materially fewer solves than the naive design with held-out quality comparable to the current order-2 result, which is the proof clause and gives the lab a propagation route for cases it currently cannot afford. Two: it bands the case but only at or near the naive cost, which says the sparsity the sensitivity result suggested is not there and the lab should stop assuming concentration transfers to the basis. Three: the higher-dimensional band comes out much wider than the five-dimensional one, which would mean the four omitted coefficients matter and the existing flat-plate band understates the coefficient channel, and that is a correction to a published number rather than a methods result. The subspace consistency check separates a genuine finding from an implementation error in every branch.
sequencing: Slow-burn, dispatchable in principle now and subordinate to the Ladder V queue under strategy rule 1; not one of the three post-send items under rule 2.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Polynomial chaos maturity: adaptive/sparse PCE beyond order-2 -> PROOF: dimension >5 case banded at tractable cost.' Operationalised: the case is the same flat plate at the same mesh with all nine source coefficients varied, so dimension is 9 and the comparison basis is measured rather than assumed; tractable cost means banding the drag coefficient with a held-out predictive score no worse than the existing order-2 result at materially fewer solves than the naive full order-2 design of about 110, with both numbers reported; the basis must be selected adaptively or sparsely from the data rather than fixed by total degree; and the nine-dimensional surrogate restricted to the five coefficients varied before must reproduce the existing order-2 answer within its own held-out error, with a failure of that check treated as an implementation defect rather than a finding.
